teaser.heading: The hand behind the needle.
teaser.lead: Tomasz works out of a quiet studio in Poland, drawing from nordic mythology, medieval woodcuts, and decades of folk ornament. Every piece is hand-drawn before it ever meets skin.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.body: Tomasz started tattooing in 2014 after years of sketching in margins and carving lino blocks at night. What began as a fascination with the engravings of Albrecht Dürer turned into a focused practice rooted in linework, stippling, and the iconography of the north.

chapters.title: Craft
chapters.body: Each session begins with a long conversation. He asks about the story behind the piece before the pencil moves. Stencils are revised on-skin until they feel inevitable. Sessions are unhurried — the line decides the pace, not the clock.

chapters.title: Influences
chapters.body: Old Norse rune-stones. Polish folk paper-cuts. Black-metal record sleeves. The texture of a winter forest at dusk. He cites Gustaf Tenggren and Theodor Kittelsen as much as he cites his own grandfather's woodworking tools.

chapters.title: Studio
chapters.body: Private studio, single chair, by appointment only. No walk-ins, no flash. Sterile, single-use, and as quiet as you want it to be.
